title: The complete guide to packshot photography, 5: how to get more professional and consistent photos
h1: The complete guide to packshot photography, 5
metaTitle: Professional Product Photos: Packshot Photography Guide
description: Learn how to take professional photos of your products in this 5th article of our packshot photography guide.
author: PackshotCreator
content:
Welcome to the 5th and final article in our series The complete guide to packshot photography. Today, we are going to discuss a crucial point for any business that wants to stand out from its online competitors: the consistency and uniformity of your packshot photos. Indeed, keeping all your product photos consistent and uniform over the long term creates an impression of high quality for your products, as well as a much more professional brand image. In this article, we will explain what to take into account during your photo shoots to ensure this consistency, then we will present the different options available to you to make this process easier. And as the saying goes, the devil is in the details!

Homogeneity and packshot photography: the secret to professional photos

Why is consistency essential for professional photos?

When you start selling products online, good presentation is essential to attract customers and convince them to buy: it is a point we have made again and again throughout this series. And consistency is part of good presentation... In fact, it is even one of the most important principles in packshot photography as soon as you have more than one product to present and sell. If the photos are not consistent with each other, you can quickly lose credibility and damage your brand image. Even worse, it can really hinder the shopping experience and drive your users away. For example, imagine that you were looking to buy shoes online and came across a website presenting these products like this:

‍

‍

If each pair of shoes is presented with different staging, inconsistent lighting and backgrounds in multiple colors, you may quickly find it hard to compare the products with each other and to get a clear idea of the product you are going to buy. This could discourage you and push you to look for products elsewhere, which is perfectly understandable. This is why visual consistency is important to create a pleasant user experience and make product comparison easier. To guarantee this consistency, it is therefore important to make sure that every detail is the same from one photo shoot to the next, details such as:

  • lighting,
  • the position of the product,
  • camera settings,
  • and the background.

‍

If any of these elements differ from one photo to another, it can create a sense of confusion and inconsistency. As you can see, to sell products online effectively, it is essential to create a smooth, high-quality user experience. Having consistent photos for each product is a key element of this experience, making it easier to compare different products and create a strong and identifiable brand image.

How to ensure consistency between all your photos for a professional result?

First, make sure that all photos are taken under the same conditions of lighting, focus and background. That means you should use the same light type, focal length, settings and background for each photo. If you're working with a professional photographer, make sure they know exactly what you expect and check their results during the photo shoot. Then, use editing software to adjust the contrast, color and sharpness of each photo, while keeping the natural appearance of the products photographed. This will allow you to standardize all of your packshot photos for a professional look. However, be careful not to over-retouch the images, or you risk misleading your customers.

‍

‍

Finally, use a template or grid to place all the products photographed in exactly the same place in the frame. This will make cropping easier and avoid confusion between different products. We also encourage you to read the 2nd article in this series, on the equipment and the concepts you need to know, where we went into more detail on the need to draw up a precise plan for the placement of your lights and equipment, so that you can always reposition them at exactly the same distances. By following these few tips, you can more easily ensure consistency between the packshot photos on your e-commerce site. You will thus give your customers a professional and consistent image, making them want to buy your products with confidence. We only have one question left to ask you, but it's a big one: How are you going to take your packshot photographs?

What solution should you choose to photograph your products according to your needs?

Are you going to outsource your packshot photography to a service provider, set up a traditional photo studio on your premises and hire a freelancer, or invest in an automated photo studio? No single solution is necessarily superior to the others. It all depends on how much time and money you want to spend on it: each of these solutions has its merits, but also its drawbacks. Let's look at each of them.

Solution 1: send your products to have them photographed externally

The first possible solution is to send your products to an external service provider specializing in product photography. This method has some interesting advantages. First of all, you don't need to worry about buying expensive camera equipment or setting aside space on your premises for shooting. Everything is handled off-site. You don't need extensive photography knowledge either. However, there are also significant drawbacks to consider. You will have to find a trustworthy provider, organize the logistics of sending and collecting your products, and the back-and-forth process may take longer. You could also have less control over the final rendering of your photos, unless you clearly specify your expectations and requirements in a detailed brief for your service provider. In any case, this solution can be an attractive option for businesses that are new to packshot photography and need a fast and practical way to produce quality images of their products.

Solution 2: set up a traditional photo studio and hire a freelancer

If you are looking for a more personalized solution for photographing your products, you may want to consider setting up a traditional photo studio on your premises and hiring a freelance product photographer. While this may seem expensive at first, it does have its benefits.

‍

‍

First, by having a photo studio on your premises, you have better control over the shots. You can adjust the lights and accessories as you like, and you can closely monitor the shooting process. And since the products do not leave your premises, the turnaround is shorter and you can pick them up as soon as the photos are taken. However, the initial cost can be high, as you will have to buy and install all the necessary equipment. This can take a lot of time and money, especially if you are not familiar with photography equipment. Plus, a photo studio can take up a lot of space, which can be a challenge in smaller workspaces. You will also need an experienced photographer to make the most of your brand-new photo studio... Hiring a freelance photographer may be an option, but it also means you'll have to wait until they are available, not to mention the additional costs. You will also need to do some research to find the most qualified and experienced photographer to ensure an impeccable end result. Setting up a traditional photo studio on your premises can thus offer numerous advantages in terms of shooting and improved response time, but the investment in time and money will be greater.

Solution 3: do everything in-house using an automated photo studio

Last possible solution: using an automated photo studio in-house. Not only can it be more convenient and faster, but it can also be more economical in the long term, even if it represents a real investment at the start. Indeed, when you hire an external provider to take photos of your products, or if you use an in-house photo studio with a freelancer, you must take into account all the associated costs: travel expenses, studio rental costs, photographer fees, etc. There is also often a time limit when you hire a service provider or a freelancer, which means that all photos must be taken and retouched within a certain period of time.

However, if you have an automated photo studio in-house, you can take photos of your products at any time, without having to pay additional fees. Whether it's a photographer, an employee in your marketing department or a stockroom employee, anyone can use this type of automated studio without the need for photography expertise: all you have to do is follow a short training course to learn how to use the studio. And you can take professional photos of your products at your own pace to ensure they meet your expectations and standards. In summary, with an automated photo studio like the ones from Orbitvu, you save time and money in the long run and you benefit from greater flexibility and much better control over your packshots, which in turn will also improve your productivity. In addition, these machines take up much less space on your premises than a traditional photo studio. So, even if this solution is more expensive at the start, you have everything to gain in the long run.
